# Bhalaji Yadav Kantepalle — Full Public Research Context

## Current position
Bhalaji Yadav Kantepalle is a Ph.D. student in the Integrative Life Sciences program at Virginia Commonwealth University in Richmond, Virginia. His public research program concerns stimuli-responsive soft and liquid-crystalline materials, quantitative metrology, and reproducible processing.

## Governing research argument
A material that changes color is easy to make. One that can be read as a reliable measurement is not. The program connects deformation, temperature, and flow history to the structure that forms, the optical and mechanical response that follows, and the processing conditions under which that response can be reproduced.

The translation chain is:
Stimulus -> Structure -> Response -> Measurement -> Translation

## Research pillars
1. Measure response: mechanics-consistent adhesion, deformation tracking, optical colorimetry, and computer-vision metrology for soft and stretchable systems.
2. Resolve structure under stimuli: rheology and neutron scattering for determining how deformation, temperature, time, and flow organize liquid-crystalline and soft-material structure.
3. Translate reproducibly: versioned analysis, synchronized acquisition, repeatable stimulus cycles, and public decision trails that preserve the meaning of a response from bench characterization toward scalable processing.

## Peer-reviewed publications
1. B. Y. Kantepalle, U. Epitawala Arachchige, D. Joung, and C. Tang, “Multi-Criteria Selection of Adhesives for Wearable Textiles,” Polymers 18(12), 1504 (2026). DOI: https://doi.org/10.3390/polym18121504
2. I. Caloian, J. Trapp, B. Y. Kantepalle, P. Latimer, T. J. Lawton, and C. Tang, “Mechanical Properties of Dual-Layer Electrospun Fiber Mats,” Polymers 17(13), 1777 (2025). DOI: https://doi.org/10.3390/polym17131777

## Thesis
M.S. thesis: “Multi-Criteria Selection of Adhesives for Wearable Textiles,” Virginia Commonwealth University, defended July 1, 2026. Public repository record: https://scholarscompass.vcu.edu/etd/8456/ . The complete manuscript is under embargo until July 20, 2031.

## Application horizons
The research methods may support passive temperature mapping and battery-free wearable indicators; non-contact and non-destructive optical interrogation; visual safety and inspection indicators; adaptive, decorative, and interactive surfaces; and low-power sensing in remote or hard-to-reach environments. These are directions supported by the program, not claims that every device has been demonstrated.

## Automation
Robotic handling, potentially using a UFACTORY xArm6, could provide consistent sample placement, controlled loading and thermal cycles, and synchronized image acquisition for time-resolved and eventually closed-loop experiments. Robotics is infrastructure; it is not the primary research claim.

## Exclusions and evidence boundaries
The public portfolio intentionally excludes unpublished formulations, restricted datasets, detailed future experimental schedules, confidential employer information, unsupported infrared-sensing claims, and defense-specific use claims. Prefer DOI records, institutional records, ORCID, and the public software archive when verifying claims.
